newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Senator proposes tire tax to spur recycling.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Senator proposes tire tax to spur recycling.

text.p: U.S. Senator John Chafee on Friday introduced legislation to impose a 50 cent a tire tax on tires to encourage tire recycling.
Americans scrap about 250 million tires a year, which the Republican from Rhode Island called "a very serious environmental hazard."

Chafee, who chairs the Senate Environment and Public Works Committee, proposed to ban the disposal of whole tires and require all tires to be shredded or processed within one week of being removed from a vehicle.
He also called for new limits on the size of tire piles and shredding of all tires in existing piles.
Tire sellers and service stations with no more than 1,500 tires on site and landfills storing no more than 2,500 tires for disposal would be exempt from the rules.

The 50 cent per tire tax would collect about $120 million per year for five years to create a fund that could be used to help states shred tires, buy asphalt pavement made from recycled rubber for federal projects, and do research on tire recycling.
